messages:
Tyler: Quick summary — ran a focused bench this morning: baseline kernel selector vs kernel-v2 on a replay-mix (30% long prompts, 70% short) + synthetic burst phases. Mixed win: throughput up but p99 regressed in a few cases. Posting notes + logs. PTAL.

benchbot: auto-summary: baseline: p50 38ms p95 210ms p99 480ms tps(1gpu) 27k tokens/s; kernel-v2: p50 35ms p95 190ms p99 510ms tps 29k tokens/s. Replay run shows ~3x p99 spikes at tail (not constant). Full CSV uploaded to s3://redwood-bench/1815064321/bench.csv

Maria: do we have the batch-shape distribution? my guess is the new kernels favor wider batches but tails push it over priming thresholds.

Tyler: attach: batch-shape heatmap + kernel selection map. Key bits: kernel-v2 picks tile-8 conv in many mixed-length batches which increases token throughput; however cross-attn path shows a hot loop.

Aj: flamegraph excerpt (copied):
```
# top hotspots
cross_attention_forward   42%  (hot)
kv_cache_lookup          12%
softmax_kernel           8%
```
Seems like the new path reduces GEMM cost but exposes more expensive KV pointer chasing on replay traffic.

Sara: replay harness detail — we were replaying traffic with cold-cache start for each run (to test cold starts). That means KV priming timing differs from synthetic. The p99 spikes correlate with requests that hit unprimed KV on long prefixes.

Tyler: good catch. I reran an apples->apples with the same seed but two modes: cold-prime (no priming) and warm-primed (run prefix pass). Results: kernel-v2 wins for warm-primed (p99 down 15%), loses for cold-prime (p99 up ~6%).

Keisha: autoscale notes from the capacity test earlier today: pool scale-up median = 22s (90% in 35s), new process init overhead ~430ms before serving tokens, burst-credit bank (our per-pod token credit) drained in ~3m under synthetic 2x burst pattern. Worth tuning burst-topup window.

Maria: can you paste the batch config used?

Tyler: config snippet:
```
batching:
  max_batch_tokens: 8192
  max_batch_size: 64
  batch_timeout_ms: 8
kernel_selector:
  prefer_kernel: auto
  allow_tile_swap: true
runtime_flags:
  kv_cache_prefetch: disabled
```
That runtime_flags kv_cache_prefetch was intentionally off to measure raw behavior.

Aj: when you say "tile swap" is enabled, do we have a policy that prevents swap for >512 seq? otherwise we see cross-attn regression.

Tyler: current policy does not clamp by seq len; we should try clamp to avoid costly cross-attn path for long inputs.

Sara: proposal: two followups — 1) rerun replay harness with kv_cache_prefetch=enabled and identical seeds (apples-to-apples). 2) run a kernel-selector ablation where we disable tile-swap for seq>512. If both reduce tail, we can land a mitigation.

benchbot: queued jobs: replay-warm-prime-1815064x (ETA 12m), replay-cold-prime-1815064y (ETA 18m), selector-ablate-1815064z (ETA 25m). Logs will post here.

Tyler: quick numbers from the warm-prime job that finished: kernel-v2 p99 420ms vs baseline 495ms, tokens/s +8%. Cold-prime job still shows kernel-v2 p99 525ms vs baseline 500ms.

Keisha: FYI the dedicated-pool run (2-gpu reserved) shows much smaller cold-start variance — scale-up into dedicated pool is ~6s for process to be ready (we had prewarmed images). If customers use dedicated pools, the cold-prime regression largely disappears.

Maria: important for docs/benching: when we compare synthetic vs replay, we must state cache priming model (cold vs warm), batch-shape distribution, and kernel selection flags. Otherwise apples-to-oranges.

Tyler: agreed. Action items:
- (Tyler) run selector-ablate + kv_prefetch enabled on replay-mix and post heatmaps (today)
- (Aj) produce flamegraphs for long-prefix subset (this afternoon)
- (Keisha) tweak burst-topup window in testbed to 30s and rerun capacity soak (tomorrow)
- (Sara) update perf guide with priming explicitness note

Sara: small note — add a test that primes KV with the first 2 tokens of frequent prefixes (cheap) and see tail change. quick win maybe.

Tyler: thanks. will post follow-ups when jobs complete. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deploy triggered: runtime/patch/kernel-v2-toggle -> staging (rollout 10%) by tyler (ops).

Keisha: ping if you want me to run dedicated-pool comparison matrix vs shared. I can schedule.

Tyler: please do, thx everyone.
